subject: Data processing footprint, subprocessors, and EU-only processing options
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@aurorahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ivy Patel <ivy.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Processing locations + subprocessors — quick Qs

Rachel —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As we dig into procurement, two compliance items bubbled up we need clarified before legal will sign:

1) Exactly where does Redwood execute inference for hosted customers by default (region / country)? Do requests ever transit outside of that region?
2) Which subprocessors (cloud infra, telemetry, logging, observability) touch inference request payloads or logs? Are any of those subprocessors located outside the EU for EU customers?
3) Do you offer an EU-only execution option (no US processing) for regulated PII? If so, what are the steps and timeline to enable it for a pilot?

Can you share a short evidence packet (one-pager with regions + subprocessors, and any artifacts we can attach to our security review)?

Appreciate quick visibility — we have a compliance checkpoint on Friday.

—Oliver
Director of IT Risk, Aurora Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ivy Patel <ivy.patel@aurorahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T10:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Processing locations + subprocessors — quick Qs

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear list. I put Karthik and Marissa (our infra/security leads for EU deployments) on copy — short answers below and we will attach a one-page pack and the subprocessor inventory. See the attached stubs.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Default hosted customers: primary inference execution runs in our US-hosted fleet (us-east-1 / us-west-2). Requests may traverse intermediate cloud regional edges for routing, but payload processing occurs in the region selected for the customer.
- Subprocessors: infra = AWS (primary), GCP (region-specific Dedicated), telemetry = Datadog, logging = Elastic Cloud (encrypted at rest), CDN = FastEdge Networks. We will provide a full CSV with locations.
- EU-only option: Yes — Dedicated or Private deployments can be provisioned to run exclusively in EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). For hosted customers we offer a regional pinning option under enterprise terms; activation requires a short onboarding checklist and a two-week SLA window for capacity assignment.

I'll let Marissa drop the explicit processing map and the inventory CSV (we'll mark which subprocessors handle persisted data vs transient telemetry). One ask — can you confirm whether Aurora requires KMS/HSM attestations and whether SOC 2 reports should be included in the packet?

Best,
Rachel
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-residency-summary-20260603.pdf (summary), subprocessor_inventory_20260603.csv (inventory)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@aurorahealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ivy Patel <ivy.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T12:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Processing locations + subprocessors — quick Qs

Oliver / Ivy —

Adding technical detail to what Rachel summarized. Attaching a simple processing map for the EU-only option (processing-map-eu-option.png). Key points below — will keep this short and factual for legal: 

1) Execution loci (what actually runs inference):
- Hosted (default): customer can choose a home region at signup. Historically our default is US regions; for EU customers we recommend selecting eu-west-1 to minimize cross-border hops.
- Dedicated / Private: can be provisioned to run exclusively in EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). In those deployments all inference execution, KV-Cache, and ephemeral storage remain in customer-chosen EU zones.

2) Data transit and persistence:
- Transit: Control plane signals (scheduling, metrics) may be routed via our control plane (control-plane.redwood.com) located in the US; these are metadata-only and can be configured to use a private peering for Dedicated/Private.
- Persistence: Model artifacts and KV cache are kept in the deployment region. Logs that contain PII are redacted by default; debug logs containing payloads are only retained if explicitly enabled and are then stored in the same region or in a customer-controlled bucket for Private deployments.

3) Subprocessors and their roles (summary):
- AWS (EC2/EBS/S3): primary compute and object storage for hosted and Dedicated (regional).
- GCP (GCE/GCS): used for some EU Dedicated capacity when preferred by customer.
- Elastic Cloud (logging): stores application logs; indices are region-scoped.
- Datadog: telemetry/metrics; we support self-hosted telemetry for high-compliance customers.
- FastEdge Networks: edge routing/caching; does not persist request payloads.
- Key management: customers can bring their own keys via AWS KMS or external HSM for Private deployments.

4) EU-only guarantees / activation steps (pilot):
- Contract addendum to pin region + subprocessors: sign-off (3–5 business days).
- Capacity reservation & infra provisioning: 7–10 business days (shorter if using Dedicated reserved pools).
- KMS/HSM integration and audit handshake: 3–7 business days depending on customer's KMS approach.

Evidence we can provide immediately: one-page residency summary (attached), subprocessor inventory (attached CSV), and our latest SOC 2 Type II report (we will share a redacted copy under NDA). If you need a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with EU-specific clauses, we can supply a template.

Next steps suggestion: if Aurora needs an EU-only pilot we can provision a constrained Dedicated pool for proof-of-concept and run a short verification test (sample requests + telemetry proof) within two weeks of contract addendum.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: processing-map-eu-option.png, export-controls.md (inline reference)

Thanks — that is helpful and covers most of our asks. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- Please include the SOC 2 Type II and the DPA template (we can review under our standard NDA).
- For the EU-only pilot, can we get a firm timeline and a named engineer for onboarding? Our compliance lead wants a single point of contact.

If you can get those to us by end of day tomorrow we'll be in a good spot for Friday's checkpoint.

Ivy and I are available for a short call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

—Oliver
